sources.title: Sylvain Arlot and Alain Celisse, A survey of cross-validation procedures for model selection, Statistics Surveys 4 (2010), author version arXiv:0907.4728
sources.locator: Full author-version PDF fetched; inspected relevant ranges §1.1; §§2.3–2.4; §§4.2.1–4.3.2; §5.1.1; §6.1; §7.1; §8.3. The journal article is Statistics Surveys 4 (2010), printed pp. 40–79.

retrieval_history.outcome: Direct publisher PDF request returned a 1,159-byte Incapsula HTML anti-bot page, not the publication.
Author-hosted course copy was found, but curl rejected the TLS certificate because the certificate subject was euler.wss.yale.edu rather than www.stat.yale.edu.
Successful same-work author-version PDF retrieval; 40 pages inspected at the listed sections.

contents.name: IID risk framework: measurable statistical algorithms and loss on an independent new observation (§1.1)
contents.reason: The local definition states its measurable learning-rule, loss-integrability, product-law, and independent-test hypotheses explicitly.

contents.name: Model-selection objectives for estimation and identification, and their distinction (§§2.3–2.4)
contents.reason: The local definition keeps prediction-risk minimization separate from recovery of a true model label and assumes neither identification nor a unique risk minimum.

contents.name: General holdout averaging, leave-one-out, leave-p-out, V-fold, and repeated split procedures (§§4.2.1–4.3.2)
contents.reason: The algorithm gives explicit training sets, validation sets, weights, and an exogenous randomization law for each retained procedure.

contents.name: Expected CV risk is the risk at the training sample size, with bias relative to full-sample risk (§5.1.1)
contents.reason: The local proof derives the training-size identity for each split and then averages with the declared schedule weights; the survey gives the holdout expectation and general split-average formulation. The local argument also handles unequal fold sizes and independent randomized schedules without asserting a bias sign.

contents.name: Risk-estimation accuracy and model-selection accuracy need not rank procedures the same way (§6.1)
contents.reason: The distinction motivates the local definition; no procedure-ranking or asymptotic optimality theorem from the survey is imported.

contents.name: Conditions for model-consistent cross-validation identification (§7.1)
contents.reason: The assigned inventory contains the objective distinction and a finite nonidentifiability example, but no asymptotic model-consistency theorem or its additional separation and rate hypotheses.

contents.name: Cross-validation under time-series and dependent observations (§8.3)
contents.reason: The B example computes a grouped-data failure and explicitly marks that it violates the IID row assumption rather than transferring the IID expectation theorem.

contents.name: Majority-vote CV selection as a separate identification-oriented rule (§4.2.2)
contents.reason: The assigned algorithm specifies the requested average-score holdout and resampling procedures; a distinct voting selector is not part of the approved item inventory.

sources.title: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, and Robert Tibshirani, An Introduction to Statistical Learning, 7th printing, Chapter 5
sources.locator: Full author-hosted book PDF fetched; inspected Chapter 5 §§5.1.1–5.1.4, printed pp. 176–184, including validation-set, LOOCV, k-fold definitions, training-size effects, repeated split variability, and the model-assessment/model-selection distinction.

contents.name: Validation-set holdout and the smaller training set's effect on estimated test error (§5.1.1)
contents.reason: The example computes an exact nonzero risk difference for a Bernoulli sample-mean predictor rather than relying on the book's empirical illustration.

contents.name: LOOCV, k-fold CV, their averaging formulas, and repeated random partition variability (§§5.1.2–5.1.3)
contents.reason: The algorithm states each procedure's exact finite split schedule and averaging weights.

contents.name: Bias–variance tradeoff for k-fold selection and the distinction between estimating test error and locating a risk minimum (§5.1.4)
contents.reason: The local lemma derives the dependence terms explicitly; it does not import the chapter's qualitative ranking of LOOCV and k-fold variance.

contents.name: Model assessment versus model selection (§5 introduction)
contents.reason: The local definition states the two objectives and the B example verifies a finite failure of identification.

contents.name: Data leakage from preprocessing or repeatedly consulting a held-out test set
contents.reason: The assigned leakage example isolates grouped-row dependence and a wrong sampling unit; preprocessing and repeated test-set consultation are separate mechanisms not claimed here.

sources.title: Yoshua Bengio and Yves Grandvalet, No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation, Journal of Machine Learning Research 5 (2004), 1089–1105
sources.locator: Full 17-page JMLR PDF fetched and inspected. §§2.1–2.5, 3, and 4 through Theorem 6 and its proof, printed pp. 1090–1098. The proof is under the paper's symmetric-algorithm, IID, fixed balanced K-fold setup.

contents.name: Prediction error and expected prediction error at the stated training size (§§2.1–2.3)
contents.reason: The local definition states $R_k$ using an independent test observation, and the bias theorem proves which training size the fixed-fold average targets.

contents.name: Matched-pair foldwise model comparison (§2.4)
contents.reason: The algorithm computes candidate loss differences under a shared split schedule, and the B example verifies their covariance on a finite Bernoulli sample.

contents.name: Three covariance classes and the exact K-fold score variance formula (Lemma 1, Corollaries 2–3, §§2.5–3)
contents.reason: The local lemma proves block-permutation invariance, pair counts, and the resulting variance identity under finite second moments.

contents.name: Theorem 6: no universally unbiased K-fold variance estimator (§4)
contents.reason: The item supplies a local finite-support polynomial-degree proof for one symmetric learner and every Bernoulli law, including estimators based on the full sample.

contents.name: Lemma 4 analytic-series restriction and Lemma 5 quadratic-form reduction (§4)
contents.reason: The source proof invokes an analytic-estimator expansion; that restriction is not used here because the local finite-support argument proves the witness claim for arbitrary measurable data-based estimators.

contents.name: Simulation study of variance estimators and empirical error-bar performance (§7)
contents.reason: Simulation outcomes are empirical illustrations and are not needed for the finite-sample covariance identity or the local nonexistence proof.
